# ADR 0003: White-label brands through a typed brand composition, generated by Tuist

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-14

## Context

The project ships three apps (SleepGuard, SleepGuard Lite, Nocturne) from one codebase. OneApp does this for seven brands and shows what to keep and what to avoid:

- Keep: real app targets; a brand links only the vendor adapters it uses; a `NoOp` adapter where a brand lacks a capability.
- Avoid: bindings that are `fatalError("Register in App composition")` until a brand's imperative DI file overrides them (a missing one crashes at launch); ~80% identical per-brand DI files; `Configuration.app == .someBrand` inside domain policies; same-named classes swapped by target membership; a hand-edited 28k-line project file with per-file membership.

## Decision

- **Tuist generates the app targets from one brand list.** The project file is not committed.
- **A brand is one folder** (`Brand.swift`, assets, xcconfig, entitlements) plus one list entry.
- **`BrandComposition` is a protocol** with a `BrandConfiguration` value (name, URL scheme, app group, theme, tabs, capabilities) and the few factory methods that differ per brand. A missing binding is a compile error.
- **Capabilities are plain flags read in two places:** coordinators and composers. There is no brand enum.
- **Theme is a value in the SwiftUI environment**, supplied by the brand and injected by the hosting controller.
- **Adapters are split by framework** so Lite does not link HealthKit.

## Consequences

- Adding a brand does not touch shared modules. A test bootstraps every brand and resolves every registration.
- Features and domain cannot branch on brand: they never receive one.
- Previews and tests pick any theme without globals.
- **Costs:**
  - Tuist is a tool to install and learn; contributors run `tuist generate`.
  - Capability flags multiply if every small difference becomes one. Prefer a value a brand supplies over a flag, and delete flags no brand sets differently.
  - Per-brand screens (not just flags) are not designed for. If one is needed, it needs a new decision.
  - All three apps share one string catalog; brand-specific wording is limited to the brand name as an argument.

## Alternatives

- **One target, brand chosen by build configuration.** Fewer targets, but different entitlements and linked frameworks per brand become conditional settings, and "a real buildable app per brand" is the requirement.
- **OneApp's placeholder-and-override DI.** Works, fails at runtime instead of compile time.
- **Asset-catalog theming by target membership.** No code, but themes can't be swapped in previews or tests and typography can't differ.
